title: The Deadmines
body: The Deadmines lie beneath Moonbrook in southern Westfall. They were once the richest gold mines in the human lands, and a Stormwind mining crew was still at work in them when a tunnel came down and buried most of its men. Now the Defias Brotherhood holds them as its secret hideout, the place its highest ranks keep to, out of the militia's sight. Defias miners still cut the rock, goblins labor in the deeper workings, and something is being built at the bottom.

parts.body: The red bandana marks every member of the Brotherhood, but the cloth tells rank, and the silk ones, worn by its highest, are found here.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Deadmines_(original), official description cited to the Battle.net zone page (once the greatest gold production center in the human lands; the Defias turned the dark tunnels into their private sanctum); the same text is npc_text 7187 (broadcast 9892: goblins rumored conscripted to build something at the bottom of the mines, what it is still uncertain), which no gossip menu uses, so it stands only beside the wiki

parts.body: The crew lost in the collapse did not stay buried. Its men walk the fallen tunnels still as skeletal miners, excavators and dynamiters.

title: The Mast Room and the Goblin Foundry
body: Deep in the Deadmines the Brotherhood's goblins do its building. In the Mast Room woodcarvers cut and shape timber under Sneed the Lumbermaster, who oversees them from the cockpit of a logging shredder, and in the Goblin Foundry craftsmen melt ore under Gilnid the Smelter. Everything they make is carried down to the bottom of the mine.

title: Ironclad Cove
body: At the bottom of the Deadmines an iron-clad door shuts off Ironclad Cove, a sea cavern hidden from the world above, and in it lies what the goblins have been building: a great ship, fitted out at docks and scaffolding. A goblin captain, a tauren first mate and a crew of Defias pirates man her, and aboard waits the master of the Brotherhood himself.

parts.body: Edwin VanCleef died on the deck of his ship, and at Sentinel Hill the People's Militia called his death the beginning of the end for the Defias Brotherhood.
